method: Reviewed reuse of prototype trajectories, re-grounded on exact canonical normalized observations. Values remain derived game estimates.
evidence_rules: Big Count mixed-sex participation is used primarily for popularity/access and is not a universal strength score.
Professional player/club evidence is competition/ecosystem context and is not a direct elite-support measurement.
Structural academy/training/youth evidence can inform development and elite support but programme launches are not treated as realised outcomes.
Outcome rankings are not promoted into automatic rating inputs in this batch.
Sparse periods remain low confidence rather than receiving fabricated neutral evidence.

country_notes.JPN: JFA history provides institutional, league, training-centre and professionalisation anchors; Big Count 2006 and FIFA Professional 2023 provide quantitative cross-sections.
country_notes.IND: Large absolute 2006 participation is separated from low organised density; modern academy/grassroots/Forward/accreditation observations support development without assuming reform targets were achieved.
country_notes.MAR: The Mohammed VI Academy timing conflict is intentionally unresolved: normalized FIFA observations state both 2009 establishment and 2019 opening. Both remain cited and modern development/support confidence is bounded.
country_notes.SEN: The 1955 period is a low-confidence pre-independence backcast; federation, academy, professional-league, youth-pathway, Big Count and professional-club observations support the modern trajectory.
